question: Should Graincrawl permanently retire the local release-artifact entry points and require the unified notarized workflow for all official publishing?
rationale: This is a deliberate operator-facing security and release-policy change: the patch is mechanically narrow, but it intentionally removes an existing publishing route and needs release-owner acceptance of that compatibility break.

options.title: Approve the unified-only release policy
options.body: Confirm that all supported official releases must use the notarized workflow, then require redacted live proof of the new failure message and snapshot fallback before merging.

options.title: Keep a supported local route
options.body: Retain or redesign a local publishing command only if maintainers need an approved recovery path outside the unified workflow.

recommendation.title: Approve the unified-only release policy
recommendation.body: Confirm that all supported official releases must use the notarized workflow, then require redacted live proof of the new failure message and snapshot fallback before merging.

likelyOwner.reason: The available context ties this person directly to the release-path proposal; local feature-history inspection was unavailable to identify a separate current-main owner.
